history.content: hi. i dont really know why im here. just feeling kind of crushed lately and needed somewhere to put it i guess
Hey. “Crushed” feels like the main thing here — maybe heavy, worn down, or just too much to carry. Does that fit at all?
yeah. crushed fits. its like everyone needs a piece of me and theres nothing left. my mom got out of the hospital two weeks ago and im the one doing everything now
That sounds like a lot landing on you at once — like everything is being asked of you and there isn’t room left for you. Is it more the amount, the responsibility, or feeling alone in it?

alone mostly. i have a brother but he just calls to ask how shes doing and then goes back to his life. im the one driving her to appointments, sorting her meds, cooking. and i still have my own kids and a job. i dont even know when i last sat down

That sounds so stretched and अके? You’re carrying the driving, meds, cooking, your kids, and your job, with barely a moment to sit down. Does it feel more like being trapped, or like being pulled in every direction?

pulled in every direction. like the second i finish one thing theres three more. and if i stop even for a minute i feel guilty, like im letting someone down. my daughter asked me to help with her science project last night and i just snapped at her. i felt awful

Pulled in every direction, and then the guilt lands on top of it — that sounds really hard. I’m wondering if the awful part is more the snapping itself, or feeling like there was nowhere else for that to go?

nowhere for it to go. thats exactly it. its all just sitting in me with no outlet. i love them all i do but im scared theres not enough of me to go around and someones gonna get the worst of me. probably already are
That sounds like a frightening kind of squeezed-in feeling — caring a lot, and also not having enough room for it anywhere else. We can stay with that, or leave it here for now; what feels right?
i think leave it here for now. i didnt expect to but just saying it out loud helped a little. ill come back. thank you
Of course — I’m glad you said it out loud, and we can leave it here. I’ll be here when you come back.
